item.statement: The alloy exhibits poor oxidation resistance at temperatures above 600 °C, with severe mass gain and eventual disintegration at 900 °C, limiting its potential applications despite good mechanical properties.
item.lever: chemical composition (reduction of V or Ti, addition of Al, Cr, or Si)
quotes: In general, the obtained results demonstrate that despite its promising mechanical properties, the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy shows rather poor oxidation resistance.
This can obviously limit the potential applications of the alloy.
At 900 °C, the specimen disintegrated after 50 h of testing.

item.statement: The presence of Vanadium hinders the formation of protective oxides and facilitates the nucleation of unprotective complex oxides, negating the potential positive effect of Aluminum on oxidation resistance.
quotes: Thus, it can be hypothesized that a possible positive effect of Al on the oxidation resistance will be neglected in the presence of V even if Al is added in high amounts.
V hinders the formation of protective oxides and facilitates the nucleation of unprotective ones.

Our results showed that a hypothetical addition of Al to the NbTiZrV does not lead to an enhancement of the oxidation resistance, but only increases the number of the unprotective complex TiNb 2 O 7 and Nb 2 Zr 6 O 17 oxides due to the AlNbO 4 oxide formation.

item.statement: The specific mechanisms driving the acceleration of oxidation at the second stage (breakaway) at 600–700 °C are not fully resolved, particularly regarding the indirect influence of V-rich oxides versus the role of Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 nucleation.
quotes: Most probably, the acceleration of oxidation at the second stage was caused by an effect similar to breakaway oxidation.
This suggests that the VO 2 and V 2 O 5 oxides had an only indirect influence on cracking/spallation at 600 °C, rather than being the main reason.

item.statement: Future work should focus on modifying the chemical composition by reducing Vanadium or Titanium and adding strong protective scale formers like Aluminum, Chromium, or Silicon to improve oxidation resistance.
item.lever: chemical composition (reduction of V or Ti, addition of Al, Cr, or Si)
quotes: To improve the oxidation resistance, modification of the chemical composition, i.e., reduction of the concentration of elements like V or Ti and/or addition or increasing of strong protective scale formers like Al, Cr, or Si is required.

Nevertheless, the information obtained in the current study can help in the design of RHEAs with a balanced combination of properties including (but not limited to) low density, high strength, sufficient ductility, and good oxidation resistance.

item.statement: The study was limited to static lab air conditions and did not test the alloy in other environments or under dynamic flow conditions, which might affect the oxidation behavior.
quotes: Oxidation tests were carried out in a Nabertherm furnace (LT 5/12/P320, Nabertherm, Lilienthal/Bremen, Germany) under static lab air at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 900 °C for 50 h.
The oxidation behavior strongly depended on the alloy composition and testing conditions.
Note that the vast majority of the performed research was conducted at temperatures of T ≥ 1000 °C.

item.statement: There is a trade-off between the high strength provided by the B2 matrix and the poor oxidation resistance caused by the formation of complex, unprotective oxides like TiNb2O7 and Nb2Zr6O17.
item.lever: phase composition (B2 matrix vs. complex oxides)
quotes: The high strength of the alloy at ambient and elevated temperatures was attributed to a strong solid solution strengthening induced by Zr and the B2 ordered matrix phase.
It was reported that the formation of the TiNb 2 O 7 and Nb 2 Zr 6 O 17 oxides had not improved oxidation resistance, whereas the AlNbO 4 oxide formation resulted in sluggish oxidation kinetics.
Apparently, the studied AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy can be considered as Al-free or V-containing analog of the NbTiZrV or AlNbTiZr alloy, respectively.

item.statement: The exact role of the Zr5Al3 particles in the oxidation front progression and pore formation requires further investigation, as they act as pathways for oxidation but also lead to void formation.
quotes: The oxidation front ascended easily along the Zr 5 Al 3 particles but was slightly impeded by the B2 phase.
In addition, a lot of pores were found at the former sites of the Zr-rich particles.
The distribution of the particles in this layer was very similar to that of the Zr 5 Al 3 particles in the substrate.

item.statement: The alloy failed to maintain structural integrity at 900 °C, disintegrating after only 50 hours, indicating that the current composition is unsuitable for this temperature range.
quotes: At 900 °C, the specimen disintegrated after 50 h of testing.
Testing at 900 °C was interrupted after 50 h due to the significant disintegration of the sample.
It can be assumed that the same processes, but in a more rapid manner, are responsible for the disintegration of the sample tested at 900 °C.
